visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md. Built from components/site/v3. No mockup in this directory: the place-type class is the city/community type-card landing, not a Tetherow one-off.
competitiveTarget: Beat Zillow / Redfin / Coldwell Banker type-filtered city results. Those surfaces dump the visitor into a search grid. This page is a place-type node: leftover count and median that already back the type card, a living atlas of the parent city with the type stated in the claim, and a photographed list of that type. Unique title, canonical, ItemList when listings exist. Breadcrumb is City then type, no Home.
note: H1 is `{Type} in {Place}` and it is the page's only display-scale line: the Atlas opens under the claim wearing an eyebrow (V3Atlas headlineTone='eyebrow', subject softened to Listings). One section-0 sourced claim sentence sits under the H1 — count and ~p90 price band from ONE listing_tile_mv read, worded as the address census with the map marking for-sale homes inside city limits (pending key hidden on this page). A V3Carousel mode=rail of photographed listings (PlaceTypeFilm; shadcn-carousel adapted with side prev/next) follows Atlas in the fold with price+address+beds/baths/sqft on 800x600 plates. The Atlas section is UNCONDITIONAL via PlaceTypeAtlasSection + PlaceTypeAtlasStandin. Rows and marks share one hovered key. Unknown type notFound(). Do not collide with app/cities/[slug]/[neighborhoodSlug].

tasteReview.beats: Zillow Bend single-family search (zillow.com/bend-or/): we win the sourced nine-in-ten asking band in one sentence and navy Atlas marks instead of Google tiles; we lose map scale, listing density, and filter power, so this is not a beat of that page. Better than a 54 because the twin Amboqia titles are gone; not a leap.

defects.section: LISTINGS INSIDE THE BEND CITY LIMITS
defects.finding: Atlas is a timid inset: Bend sits as a postage-stamp polygon in a wide unused cream field, with zoom chrome at the edge. The job of this fold is the map under one claim, occupying the first viewport, not a dashboard widget above a portal rail.

The sentence says 777 homes with a Bend address; the map reads 502 for sale. Layout lock requires count and band from the same listing-tile as the map marks. Two inventories in one fold is a trust nick even with the city-limits caption.

At 375px the second slide is sheared through the price ($1,985,0), address (3422 Jacks), and specs (4 bd · 4 ba ·). The rail is a shadcn carousel with arrows, but a clipped peek is not a composed next card.

The first viewport already has a photographed listing carousel, then a second inventory with NEWEST / PRICE LOW / PRICE HIGH / MOST BEDS. Two listing systems stacked is portal furniture; one shadcn carousel is the job.

SEO increment is not visible in these shots (no title or JSON-LD proof), so SEO is at best held. The page job of reaching a broker is only a header phone on desktop and missing on mobile. Inventory facts on the cards (price, address, beds, baths, sqft) are present; a held SEO line is a defect on this pass.

tasteReview.verdict: This is a 55: slightly better than a 54 because the stacked twin headlines are gone and the fold is H1, then a sourced count-and-band sentence, then Atlas, then a photo rail with listing facts — but Atlas is still a widget, 777 disagrees with 502, and the 375 rail clips the next house. Inventory improved on the cards; SEO is not shown to have improved, which this pass treats as a defect, and the page still does not beat Zillow Bend on map scale or listing density.
